comparator.name: Biologie (Biology)
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 Biology regulations and study guide specify a 135 EC major and 45 EC of profiling space. The major contains 75 required EC, including the 15 EC graduation project, and 60 EC of restricted Biology electives, including a first-year choice. The interest directions guide elective selection within the major. This comparison preserves the official elective space.

alternatives.label: Biological sciences: cells, organisms and ecosystems
alternatives.labelReason: The programme spans biological organisation from molecules and cells through physiology, organisms, biodiversity and ecosystems, supported by laboratory, statistical and data methods.
alternatives.concept: Study life from genes and cells to organisms and ecosystems. Connect biochemistry, physiology and disease to evolution, conservation and marine ecology. Use laboratory methods, programming and statistics to investigate biological questions.
progression: The life science gateway precedes dependent courses. Programming precedes data science, and Mathematical Methods precedes Probability & Statistics. Introductory biodiversity precedes ecology, conservation and evolution.

alternatives.label: Molecular, cellular and biomedical biology
alternatives.labelReason: Molecular-cell biology, biochemistry, genetics, immunology, physiology and experimental/data methods form a coherent health-facing biological direction supported by the programme’s cells, genomics, bioinformatics, neurobiology and health interests.
alternatives.concept: Study how cells, genes and biomolecules shape health and disease. Use laboratory methods, anatomy, physiology and neuroscience to investigate mechanisms, then apply statistics, epidemiology and computing to health evidence and biological data.
progression: The life science and brain gateways precede dependent courses. Molecular cell biology comes before molecular pathology and disease. Programming and mathematics come before applied data science, and data science precedes machine learning and deep learning.
alternatives.distinctness: This option shares molecular, physiological and evolutionary foundations with the broad option. It uses seven different courses to develop neuroscience, epidemiology and computational prediction and imaging in place of several ecology and environmental courses.

alternatives.label: Ecology, evolution and conservation biology
alternatives.labelReason: Evolution, biodiversity, ecosystems, conservation, climate, biogeochemistry and field-oriented environmental research form a coherent direction grounded in explicit programme interests and current Biology study-interest guidance.
alternatives.concept: Study how evolution and environmental change shape biodiversity. Connect conservation, marine ecology and farming to climate, soils and nutrient cycles. Use field, laboratory and statistical methods and investigate a sustainability question with a regional partner.
progression: Early biodiversity and sustainability courses support later marine ecology, conservation and biogeochemistry. The life science gateway precedes the dependent cell biology, laboratory, physiology and immunity courses. The regional partner project runs in term one and introduces guided team research.
alternatives.distinctness: This option adds eight courses to the broad option in sustainability systems, climate, farming, Earth-system methods, biogeochemistry and regional partner research. It focuses on populations, habitats and environmental change instead of concentrating on human disease and computing.

core: Living organisms and biological systems from molecules to ecosystems
Genes, genomes, cells, biomolecules and molecular mechanisms
Plants, animals, microorganisms, physiology and organismal biology
Biological modelling, statistics, genomics, bioinformatics and quantitative evidence
Experimental, laboratory, field and independent biological research
adjacent: Health, biomedical research, biotechnology and toxicology
Human impacts, environmental change and nature conservation
Neurobiology and biological bases of behaviour
questions: How do biological systems function from molecules and cells to organisms and ecosystems?
How do evolution and human activity shape biodiversity, ecosystems and conservation needs?
How can molecular, computational and experimental biology address health challenges?

candidates.label: Educational minor in biology teaching
candidates.reason: Rhetoric in Action develops lesson design and coaching through speaking work with primary-school pupils. This is useful teaching practice. The available communication and biology courses lack a sustained biology-specific teaching sequence with supervised secondary-school practice. The two selected directions have stronger disciplinary coverage.

trace: Introduces biomolecules, membranes, cell division, energy metabolism, heredity and biotechnology as foundations for life science.
Surveys the tree of life, microorganisms, plants, animals and methods for investigating biodiversity.
Builds programming foundations useful for biological data analysis and bioinformatics.
Develops molecular-cell biology, genomes, gene expression, signalling, division, tissues and current research methods.
Examines extinction, human impacts and scientific and policy responses in conservation biology.
Studies population dynamics, species interactions, energy and matter flows and ecological succession, including analysis of ecological models.
Provides mathematical techniques needed for quantitative and computational biological work.
Examines molecules, cells, tissues, organ systems, homeostasis and organismal physiology.
Covers biomolecules, metabolism, signalling and biochemical foundations of biotechnology and disease.
Studies evolutionary mechanisms from genes to populations and their application across biology.
Adds probability, distributions, sampling, estimation and simulation for biological inference.
Provides molecular and microbiological laboratory work, including proteins, PCR, electrophoresis and bioinformatics.
Studies microbes, host–pathogen interaction, innate and adaptive immunity and immunopathology.
Examines nervous system structure and function, neural signalling and behaviour using experimental and comparative perspectives.
Connects organisms and ecosystems to soil processes, water and environmental conditions.
Advances molecular genetics, mutation, inheritance, pathology, testing and treatment.
Applies molecular, cellular and physiological regulation to pharmacology and toxic effects.
Develops marine ecology across estuaries, coasts and coral reefs and assesses human impacts.
Introduces data preparation, analysis, visualisation and evidence-based computational inquiry.
Connects normal organ-system function to disease mechanisms and examines causes, diagnosis and treatment in several body systems.
Develops structure–function reasoning through human anatomy, imaging and anatomical variation.
Examines geoscience and risk reduction in hazards including droughts and toxic algal blooms, adding environmental risk context.
Adds governance, interests, public evidence and implementation for environmental and conservation action.
Introduces neurons, brain organisation, behaviour and neuroscience research methods.
Builds and evaluates neural networks for predictive and image tasks. These methods can transfer to biological data analysis.
Examines sensory and motor systems connecting neural mechanisms to perception and action.
Extends biological and cognitive analysis to advanced brain functions.
Introduces predictive modelling and machine-learning workflows for complex data.
Processes and classifies images with methods applicable to microscopy and anatomical imaging.
Introduces environmental systems, sustainability problems and interdisciplinary analysis.
Adds physical and chemical methods, including spectroscopy and microscopy, alongside materials science. Its contribution to ecology is complementary.
Provides Earth-system context for habitats, climate and long-term environmental change.
Examines climate processes, evidence, impacts and responses shaping biological systems.
Studies organisms, food systems, environmental impacts and ecological innovations in farming.
Examines chemical equilibria, mineral reactions, weathering and microbial control of redox processes in natural environments.
Develops a question, literature review, investigation and report in a small team with a regional partner. The biological content depends on the available brief.
Models Earth-system interactions and uses proxies and isotope tracers to investigate environmental and climate change.
Estimates disease frequency and risk and evaluates study design, bias, causal claims and evidence for public-health interventions.
blocks: Biological foundations: cells, organisms and diversity
Both examine cellular structure, gene expression, signalling and molecular mechanisms. UCR’s separate life science gateway supplies the introductory foundation.
Both introduce evolution and biodiversity across major groups of life.
Both address animal structure and function; UCR concentrates on human physiology.
Both study microorganisms. UCR emphasises infection and immune responses. Its biodiversity course surveys plant diversity, while Utrecht includes dedicated plant physiology.
Both combine ecological principles with modelling or experimental reasoning.
Both study genes and genomes. UCR emphasises inheritance, mutations and disease. Utrecht gives dedicated attention to genome analysis.
Utrecht requires one of two first-year Biology electives.
Molecular, cellular, physiological and biomedical biology
Students choose these courses from the Biology major list subject to level and course-entry rules.
Evolution, ecology, conservation and environmental systems
Quantitative methods, research and open study space
Both develop quantitative biological reasoning and statistics; UCR supplies a general mathematical-statistics sequence.
Utrecht requires a dedicated academic communication course. UCR develops related writing and presentation skills across courses.

Utrecht requires supervised biological research, a written report and a presentation. The ecology option includes a team partner project whose topic depends on the brief. UCR offers optional independent research separately.
Utrecht reserves 45 EC for profiling through electives or a minor.

selection.assessment: The broad option spans molecules to ecosystems. The two focused options develop distinct questions about mechanisms of disease and the response of biodiversity to environmental change. Each has a feasible 24-course plan and adds at least seven courses to the broad option.

notes.text: Utrecht combines a broad compulsory first year with restricted Biology electives and a 15 EC graduation project. UCR offers substantial overlap in cell biology, genetics, physiology, ecology and quantitative methods. Utrecht gives more dedicated attention to plant physiology and genome analysis. Its required research project differs from UCR’s team sustainability project and optional independent research.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht Biology studies living systems from molecules and cells to organisms and ecosystems. The first year covers molecular biology, plants, microorganisms, animals, evolution, ecology, genomics and statistics. Later Biology electives allow students to develop an emphasis before completing a supervised research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The broad UCR option connects cellular biology and physiology to evolution and ecology. One focused option adds disease, neuroscience and computational methods. The other adds conservation and studies how climate and human activity change ecosystems. Utrecht includes dedicated plant physiology and genome analysis and requires a 15 EC Biology research project.

curriculum.limitation: This outline preserves the restricted Biology electives and the 45 EC of profiling space. Utrecht’s study-interest directions guide choices within one Biology degree.

componentNotes.bio-y1-choice: Choose Biotechnologie en maatschappij or Introductie Mariene wetenschappen.
componentNotes.bio-major-choice: Across the 60 EC of Biology electives, complete at least 15 EC at level 2 and 30 EC at level 3, including at least 22.5 EC from the designated level 3* courses.
componentNotes.bio-graduation: Entry requires 120 EC within the Biology major, including the compulsory first-year courses and Academic Communication. Profiling courses fall outside these 120 EC.
componentNotes.bio-profiling: At least 15 of these 45 EC must be at level 2 or 3. This space can include individual electives or a minor.
